holidays.name: International Talk Like a Pirate Day
holidays.description: Every September 19, landlubbers around the world swap their normal greetings for hearty cries of 'Ahoy, matey!' and 'Arrr!' Participants pepper their conversations with pirate slang, wear eyepatches and bandanas, and generally act like swashbuckling scoundrels for the day.
holidays.origin: Started in 1995 when John Baur and Mark Summers of Albany, Oregon, were playing racquetball. One of them yelled out a pirate-style exclamation after a hit, and they decided to make it a holiday. It went global in 2002 after humorist Dave Barry wrote about it in his newspaper column.
holidays.funFact: The date, September 19, was chosen because it was the birthday of Summers' ex-wife, making it easy to remember. The holiday has also been embraced by the Pastafarian Church of the Flying Spaghetti Monster, whose followers consider pirates their divine ancestors.

holidays.name: National Butterscotch Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the silky, buttery, caramel-like dessert that often gets overshadowed by chocolate and vanilla. Fans enjoy it by the spoonful, in pies, parfaits, or topped with whipped cream.
holidays.origin: This is a food-industry-style unofficial observance, part of the many dessert days that sprang up in the United States to celebrate beloved comfort foods. Butterscotch pudding itself dates back to Victorian-era Britain.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, butterscotch contains no scotch whisky. It is made from brown sugar and butter, and the 'scotch' part may come from 'scorch' or 'score,' referring to how the candy was cut into pieces.

holidays.name: National Rice Krispies Treats Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the gooey, marshmallowy, crunchy snack that has been a lunchbox and bake sale staple for generations. People whip up batches at home, add chocolate drizzle, sprinkles, or peanut butter, and share the sticky joy.
holidays.origin: Rice Krispies Treats were created in 1939 by Mildred Day, an employee at Kellogg's, as a fundraising item for the Camp Fire Girls. The cereal itself was introduced in 1928, and the snack remains popular nearly a century later.
holidays.funFact: The famous snap, crackle, and pop sounds of Rice Krispies come from the toasted rice walls cracking when milk is poured on them. The cereal's marketing has leaned on those sounds for decades with its cartoon mascots.

holidays.name: National Cheeseburger Day
holidays.description: Burger lovers across the United States celebrate by piling melted cheese on juicy patties. Restaurants often offer deals and special sandwiches, and home cooks fire up the grill to debate the perfect cheese, whether American, cheddar, or Swiss.
holidays.origin: National Cheeseburger Day is observed on September 18 by many sources, though it is widely celebrated across the same week alongside other burger deals. The cheeseburger is said to have been invented in the 1920s or 1930s, with Lionel Sternberger of Pasadena often credited with adding cheese to a hamburger around 1926.
holidays.funFact: A patent for the name 'cheeseburger' was reportedly filed by Louis Ballast of Denver in 1935 under the Humpty Dumpty Drive-In, though the claim to the invention is disputed by several restaurants.

holidays.name: Rice Krispies Treat Creative Day (Hug a Pirate Moment)
holidays.description: A playful unofficial extension of Pirate Day, where fans combine their love of snacks and swashbuckling by hosting pirate-themed parties with treasure maps, gold coin chocolate, and plank-walking contests.
holidays.origin: This is a fan-driven tradition that grew out of Talk Like a Pirate Day gatherings, where partygoers mix food and costumes to make the day even more festive.
holidays.funFact: Real pirates of the Golden Age rarely made anyone walk the plank. That punishment is mostly a creation of fiction, popularized by stories like Peter Pan and Treasure Island.
